books.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
books.author: Daniel Kahneman
books.intro: An exploration of the two systems that shape human thought: fast, intuitive judgment and slow, deliberate reasoning. Kahneman shows how cognitive biases influence everyday decisions.

books.title: Design as Art
books.author: Bruno Munari
books.intro: Munari argues that good design should be beautiful, functional, and accessible. Through everyday objects and visual examples, he explores where art and modern design meet.

books.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
books.author: Ted Chiang
books.intro: Eight science-fiction stories blend rigorous ideas with deeply human questions about language, memory, free will, and identity. The collection includes the story that inspired Arrival.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/Stories of Your Life and Others.png

books.title: How to Take Smart Notes
books.author: Sönke Ahrens
books.intro: A practical introduction to the Zettelkasten method for building a network of connected ideas. It shows how better notes can support clearer thinking, lasting learning, and more efficient writing.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/How to Take Smart Notes.png

books.title: The Vegetarian
books.author: Han Kang
books.intro: After disturbing dreams, Yeong-hye stops eating meat, turning a private choice into an act of rebellion against her family and society. Her transformation exposes violence, control, and the fragile boundary between human and natural life.

books.title: The Borrowed
books.author: Chan Ho-Kei
books.intro: Six interconnected cases trace legendary detective Kwan Chun-dok's fifty-year career. Told in reverse, the mysteries also form a portrait of Hong Kong through decades of political and social change.

books.title: The House Where I Died Once With Obi
books.author: Keigo Higashino
books.intro: A woman with no memories of her childhood visits an isolated house with her former boyfriend, hoping to recover her past. Inside, an old diary and a home frozen in time lead them toward a disturbing family secret.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/The House Where I Died Once.png

books.title: Ark
books.author: Yuki Haruo
books.intro: Ten hikers become trapped in a flooding underground bunker with only one escape route, and one person must be left behind. When murder strikes, survival becomes a locked-room mystery.

books.title: Klein Bottle
books.author: Kodansha Bunko
books.intro: A young writer joins the testing of an astonishing virtual-reality game built from his own story. When his fellow tester disappears, the line between the simulation and the real world begins to collapse.

books.title: The Seventh Day
books.author: Yu Hua
books.intro: After dying without money for a burial, Yang Fei wanders the afterlife for seven days and encounters people he once lost. His journey becomes a surreal portrait of love, inequality, and a rapidly changing China.

books.title: Small Team Management Manual for Less than 10 People
books.author: Katsuhiko Horinouchi
books.intro: A practical guide for first-time managers leading teams of fewer than ten people. It covers setting goals, motivating different personalities, and balancing leadership with hands-on work.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/Small Team Management Manual for Less than 10 People.png

books.title: Holy Mother
books.author: Akiyoshi Rikako
books.intro: After a child is brutally murdered in her town, Honami becomes fiercely protective of her young daughter and increasingly distrustful of the police. The mystery asks how far a mother will go to keep her child safe.

books.title: The World According to Garp
books.author: John Irving
books.intro: A darkly comic account of writer T. S. Garp and his unconventional mother, feminist icon Jenny Fields. Their turbulent lives explore family, sexuality, violence, and the unpredictable collision of comedy and grief.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/The World According to Garp.png

books.title: Fight Club
books.author: Chuck Palahniuk
books.intro: An alienated office worker falls under the spell of Tyler Durden and their secret underground boxing club. The club grows into a violent rebellion against consumer culture and modern emptiness.

books.title: A Man Called Ove
books.author: Fredrik Backman
books.intro: Ove is a rigid, grieving curmudgeon whose carefully ordered life is disrupted by a lively new family next door. Their unexpected friendship reveals the tenderness behind his anger and the lasting impact one person can have.

books.title: Journey Under the Midnight Sun
books.author: Keigo Higashino
books.intro: An unsolved murder in 1970s Osaka links two children whose lives unfold along separate but shadowed paths for the next twenty years. A persistent detective follows the case through an intricate story of secrecy, ambition, and devotion.
books.cover: shelf/book cover/Journey Under the Midnight Sun.png
